public_rationale: Epoch's November 10, 2025 research describes timelines of 1–3.6 years from construction start to 1 GW of facility power, including projected milestones [e1]. JLL's January 5, 2026 report gives an 18-month global average build time for 50 MW data centers, without isolating AI facilities [e2]. Neither source establishes representative actual construction-to-operation durations for new AI data centers applicable to September 1–29, 2026, so they do not settle whether the typical duration reached two years [e1, e2].
limitations: Projected milestones do not establish completed construction durations.
The sources cover different project sizes and completion milestones.
The evidence does not provide a representative sample matching the target period and AI-specific scope.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers take years to build.

statement.excerpt: AI data centers take years to build.

our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns typical new AI data center construction, not an assertion that every retrofit or equipment installation takes years.
Read years as a multi-year construction-to-operation interval, ordinarily at least two years.
Measure from construction commencement to operational readiness. Planning, grid queues, initial operation and full-campus completion must be distinguished.
Use September 1–29, 2026 as the current observation window because the passage describes the buildout as it stood when posted.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence of construction durations applicable to the target period shows that new AI data centers typically require at least two years to become operational.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative comparable evidence shows that new AI data centers typically become operational in less than two years.
